subject: Data locality & region pinning — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <s.liu@acme-bio.com>

Cc: acme-bio-security@acme-bio.com

Subject: Follow-up: data handling questions after today's demo

Hi Ben + Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — that helped us understand Redwood's runtime and the latency guarantees. Our security and infra teams asked me to capture a few follow-up questions so we can move toward a technical review. High level items below; I'll attach a spreadsheet with some DPA/DPS questions we've been tracking.

Priority questions:
- PII handling: If we send sensitive user content into Redwood for inference, what are the contractual & technical controls to ensure we never store PII (beyond short-lived caches)? Do you have a documented data flow for PII?
- Data retention & logs: How long do request logs and token payloads persist in hosted mode by default? Is there a legal/contract option to shorten retention or disable certain logs?
- Region pinning: We want EU-only persistence for EU users. Can customers pin model endpoints and backups to a region (e.g., eu-west-1) and ensure backups/snapshots are resident only in that region? What about read-only cross-region replicas for disaster recovery?
- Cross-region failover: If a region goes down, what is Redwood's recommended failover pattern that balances residency requirements vs. availability? Is there an automated cross-region failover that still respects data residency (e.g., failover to a standby in the same political region)?
- Encrypted backups & KMS: Are snapshots encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK)? How do you handle key residency?

Can we get short answers to the bullets above and a suggested agenda for a 30-minute follow-up with your security engineer + our security lead (Tom Erickson, cc'd once he joins)?

I've attached DPA_questions.xlsx with some legal-side items.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director of Cloud & Security
Acme Bio

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized answers below and proposed concrete next steps so we can get your security team the artifacts they need. Attaching a short one-pager (data_handling_summary.pdf) that hits the same bullets for sharing with legal.

Quick answers (short):
- PII handling: By default Redwood does not persist model outputs beyond session/kv cache TTLs. For hosted customers we offer a contractual DPA and an option to disable persistent request logging. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can opt for no persistent storage of user input (ephemeral-only) and control via config.
- Data retention & logs: Default request/log retention is 30 days in hosted mode; we can offer retention options down to 0 days for enterprise customers under contract or immediately for Dedicated/Private. Logging of token payloads can be disabled; audit logs remain but can be limited to metadata only.
- Region pinning & backups: Customers can pin endpoints and their backups to a single region. For EU-only persistence we support region-scoped backups (snapshots stored and encrypted in the chosen AWS region). Cross-region backups are opt-in and are disabled by default for pinned endpoints.
- Cross-region failover: For customers with strict residency, we recommend active-standby within the same political/geo boundary (e.g., eu-west-1 primary with eu-west-2 standby) and not failing over to a different geopolitical region. We also support read-only replicas in other regions for latency (opt-in). Auto-failover to a different region is possible but requires a residency exception.
- Encryption & KMS: Snapshots are encrypted at rest; we support BYOK with AWS KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers CMK integration is available for enterprise contracts; key residency follows the region where the CMK is created.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Share data_handling_summary.pdf and the short compliance appendix for your legal/security review (attached).
2) Schedule 30 min with Jordan (security engineer), Marissa (enterprise CS), and your security lead Tom to walk the DPA items and confirm desired retention/pinning.
3) If you want, we can spin up a temporary sandbox tenant pinned to eu-west-1 (and a us-east-1 sandbox) for testing in the next 48–72 hrs.

Are you available next Tue/Wed for the meeting? If you prefer, Jordan can also send a short technical appendix with the exact console steps and API snippets.

Thanks — talk soon.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: data_handling_summary.pdf (1 page)

Hi Sarah — Jordan here, I'm the solutions engineer Ben mentioned. Quick technical clarifications to the three bullets Sarah flagged:

1) Region-scoped backups: When you choose to pin an endpoint to a region we configure storage ACLs and our backup pipeline to write snapshots to the selected region's object storage. For hosted customers we do not replicate those snapshot objects to other regions unless the customer explicitly opts into cross-region backup. We will provide a short appendix to the DPA that states that Redwood will not perform cross-region replication for pinned endpoints without customer authorization. That appendix can be signed as part of the DPA.

2) Residency exception & failover: The residency exception is a documented approval path that requires (a) signed change request from a named customer security contact, (b) explicit acceptance of the temporary residency deviation window, and (c) a rollback plan. Automated cross-region failover that violates residency is off by default; we can enable a managed failover policy for critical outages but it requires the exception and impacts SLA measurement (we track both RTO and any post-failover compliance windows). For most customers with strict residency we recommend active-standby in the same geopolitical region.

3) BYOK and key lifecycle: Yes — we can integrate your CMK in eu-west-1 and give your team rotation control via IAM/KMS policies. If you deprovision keys on your side we will mark the snapshots unreadable and follow the agreed retention/deletion schedule; Redwood's standard process for key revocation and data access termination will be included in the compliance appendix.

Practical next steps from my side: 
- I'll draft the DPA appendix language and post it to the Drive folder by EOD.
- Ben, please pick two meeting slots for Wed/Thu mornings CET and I'll link the invite.
- We can also spin up an eu-west-1 sandbox and share access credentials with Tom for hands-on validation.

Looking forward to the meeting.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
